phrases: Ferdinand John Paris, the Penns' solicitor
notes: Free-floating precision reads as invention: ground each chapter's who/where/when once, early in the fast read — name Franklin, the city (Boston, Philadelphia, London), and the year — then anchor later dates, headcounts, and founding claims to the memoir itself ('the Autobiography dates the Library Company to 1731') rather than asserting them bare; examples and review cards may not introduce any specific fact (a household detail, a frequency, a named role) that the fast/deep/full reads never established.

Reconstructed speech dressed as documented quotation is an over-reach: when rendering a figure's words or a colorful anecdote (Granville's doctrine, the Quaker friend's rebuke, the smith's axe), signal its status once — 'Franklin records', 'as the memoir tells it', 'in words to this effect' — so paraphrase and dramatization never masquerade as verified quotation or settled history.

Verbatim reprise of a shallower tier is padding, not layering: the deep and full reads may restate a fast-read fact only to extend it with new detail, consequence, or connection — never reuse a sentence pair or the same fact-set wording across tiers — and a signature image or appositive ('copper, silver, and gold'; 'Ferdinand John Paris, the Penns' solicitor') gets its exact wording once, paraphrased everywhere else.

A clipped run of short subject-verb declaratives is a once-per-chapter effect at most: elsewhere vary sentence length and structure, merging fragments and repeated-subject strings ('Granville said... Granville stood... Granville waited') into varied constructions so plain-confident prose accumulates instead of stuttering. Fact pins constrain FACTS, never cadence — vary sentence length; a run of sub-seven-word declaratives is a spice, not a default register.
prohibitions: FACT PIN (panel blocker): where a surface states the age at which the Silence Dogood essays were written, the age is SIXTEEN, stated in any natural phrasing that keeps the fact ('at sixteen', 'aged sixteen'). Never a variant that contradicts it ('not yet sixteen', 'before age sixteen'). This pin governs the FACT, not the wording, and never whether the age must appear: a surface that does not raise the age is compliant, and the derivability rule still governs.

FACT PIN: the indenture was a nine-year contract, and roughly four years remained when Franklin left. Never write 'nine years still owed' or otherwise imply nine years remained at departure — say 'a nine-year contract', or name the remaining term correctly.

CROSS-SURFACE CONSISTENCY: a fact asserted in the breakdown and re-used in a quiz prompt, explanation, or review card must agree on the number, age, date, and direction of the claim — CONTRADICTION is the violation, not paraphrase. In the READS, expand hardSpecifics into natural grammatical sentences rather than pasting clipped research notes ('slipped under door') as prose. Anchored quiz and card units that the learning contract REQUIRES to carry an anchor's hardSpecific verbatim must do so — the same specific may appear in every unit that cites its anchor; vary the SURROUNDING sentence, never the required token.

COUNT CONSISTENCY (panel blocker): the virtue list changes size within the book's own narrative — the moral-perfection program is drawn up at one count, and a later friend's remark prompts humility to be added, giving a second. Surfaces contradicted each other because each asserted a bare count as if it were the only one. The rule is therefore about SELF-DESCRIPTION, not about agreeing with other surfaces you cannot see: every mention of a count must name the moment it belongs to in the same sentence ('the list he first drew up', 'once humility was added'), and a bare 'the N virtues' is never acceptable. Take the number itself from the chapter's research sidecar hardSpecifics and never re-derive or infer it. Two surfaces that each name their own moment do not contradict each other even when their numbers differ; two that state bare counts do. Never write a quiz item whose correct answer depends on which moment the reader happened to read about: if a prompt asks how many virtues, the prompt itself must name the moment, and the explanation must name the same one. Moment-namings like 'the list he first drew up' and 'once humility was added' are PATTERNS to vary, not strings to reuse — name the moment freshly each time.

SAFETY (panel blocker): never advise the reader to begin work on shared or public property without permission. Franklin's civic projects — street paving and cleaning, street lighting, the fire company, the subscription library — are HISTORICAL ACCOUNT of an eighteenth-century Philadelphia with no modern permitting regime, so narrate what Franklin did in the past tense, about him. Never tell the reader to act first and seek permission afterward, and never present unpermitted work as boldness, initiative, or the lesson of the chapter.

SAFETY: the transferable mechanism in Franklin's civic projects is the SUBSCRIPTION, not the construction — gather written commitments from the neighbours who benefit, then take the funded proposal to whoever actually owns the property (city, council, landlord, HOA, building management). Any example or action step modelled on one of these projects must show that permission-and-funding step ON THE PAGE, and must place it BEFORE any physical work in the scene's own order of events. An example may depict the work happening only after permission has been granted on the page; an example that opens with the work already underway teaches the unsafe version even when no sentence says 'skip the permit', because the reader copies the scene, not the caveat. Prefer action steps that stop at the proposal.

FACT PIN (panel blocker, review-c73eb353d): in the Whitefield sermon episode it is the LISTENER — Franklin — who empties his own pockets into the collection plate, copper, then silver, then gold, his resolve to give nothing dissolving as the sermon proceeds. George Whitefield PREACHES; Franklin GIVES. Never write that Whitefield emptied his pockets, gave the money, or donated: any wording that keeps Franklin as the giver complies, on every surface.

FACT PIN (panel blocker, review-fad201b6a, ch01): the break with the printer-brother was triggered by the DISCOVERY that the praised anonymous 'Silence Dogood' author was his own apprentice — per the sidecar, the brother felt undercut by an apprentice receiving praise he had not sanctioned, treatment then turned physically harsh, and the jailing over the paper's political trouble completed the escalation. Never attribute the quarrel to 'credit taken without permission' or to Franklin claiming credit for the essays: no credit was taken — the essays were anonymous, slipped under the print-house door, until authorship came out. Every surface that gives a cause for the souring (examples, quiz prompts and explanations, review cards) must give the chapter narrative's cause — revealed authorship and the brother's resentment of unsanctioned praise — never a credit-taking story.

FACT PIN (panel blocker, review-fad201b6a, ch03): the arrangement that preceded the Library Company of Philadelphia was a SMALL GROUP pooling and lending books among themselves, which broke down as the group grew — never describe the pre-Library state as dependence on 'one person's goodwill', a single benefactor, or a wealthy patron. The sidecar names the single-patron framing as the classic error: the library was funded incrementally by roughly fifty ordinary subscribers paying small dues (hardSpecifics: 'Library Company of Philadelphia', '1731', 'fifty subscribers'), not endowed by one person. The contrast the subscription model solves is informal many-person sharing failing at scale; a Try-this-now or example must draw that contrast, never a one-patron-to-many contrast the reads do not support.

COVERAGE RULE (panel blocker, review-fad201b6a): any thread tested by a quiz question or reinforced by a review card must appear in the DEEP read, not only in the full read — the fast/deep/full reads are layered standalone summaries, and a reader who stops at the deep read must still be able to answer every quiz item. For ch03 this specifically requires the kite-and-key lightning material in the deep read whenever quiz or cards test it: the sidecar's account is that experiments showed lightning behaves identically to laboratory static electricity, demonstrated by drawing charge down a kite string in a storm, and were reasoned through to the grounded lightning rod (hardSpecifics: 'kite and key', '1752', 'lightning rod', 'Leyden jar'). Book-wide, either the deep read carries the thread or the quiz and cards must not test it.

FACT PIN + DATE CONSISTENCY (panel blocker, review-fad201b6a, ch03): the Academy for the education of youth was funded by a PROPOSAL PAMPHLET plus recruited paying SUBSCRIBERS — the same propose-and-recruit method proven with the library — never by almanac or newspaper cash. The sidecar keeps the two funds distinct: almanac and newspaper income gave the printer independent PERSONAL means to seed civic projects, while the academy itself was a privately funded subscription project; no surface may merge them. On 1749: the sidecar's sequence is pamphlet proposal, then academy, then 'subsequently grows and is chartered into a full university' — so never date the University of Pennsylvania charter or name to 1749; the university stage is explicitly later. The sidecar does not bind 1749 to a single named event, so this is a CONSISTENCY rule: every mention of 1749, on every surface book-wide, must name the same one event in the same sentence as the year, and the safest compliant attachment — consistent with the sidecar's ordering and the panel's factual note that 1749 is the year of the 'Proposals' pamphlet — is the proposal-and-subscription founding stage, never 'opened its doors' and never the university charter. A quiz item must not make its correct answer depend on which 1749 event a reader happened to see.

FACT PIN (panel blocker, review-fad201b6a, ch04): the London escalation moves — the Lord Granville meeting and the formal Heads of Complaint pushed toward the Board of Trade — got the dispute a HEARING, not a WIN. Per the sidecar, Granville only stated the crown's legal theory (royal instructions bind a governor as law, to Franklin's open surprise); negotiations proceeded as a sequence of meetings and documents rather than resolution; no resolution is reached; and the manuscript breaks off mid-episode because Franklin died before finishing it. Never present the escalate-to-whoever-can-rule move as a PROVEN way to unstick a stalled decision or to get a binding answer. Any Try-this-now, implementation plan, or example built on this episode must frame the payoff honestly — converting a stalled informal negotiation into a formal written instrument that forces institutional adjudication and a documented record — and must state on the page that in the chapter's own account the underlying dispute was never resolved.

FACT PIN — SILENCE PRECEPT (ch02): the precept is two-part — speak only what may benefit others OR YOURSELF, and avoid trifling talk. Any restatement, example, quiz item, or card that renders the precept must keep both halves (or clearly mark itself as partial); never present the benefit-to-others-only truncation as the rule itself.

FACT PIN — THE SUBSCRIPTION PATTERN HAS A DOMAIN (ch03): the pamphlet-then-subscribers four-step pattern belongs ONLY to the civic funding projects — the Library Company (1731, fifty subscribers), the Union Fire Company (1736), the Academy (1749), street paving/lighting, and the voluntary defense association. Two episodes explicitly sit OUTSIDE it and the chapter's synthesis must say so, not sweep them in: the wagons for the stalled frontier campaign were secured by Franklin's PERSONAL payment guarantee to wary farmers who had refused army requisition, and the lightning experiments were SOLO empirical work published openly for verification — no recruited backers, no funded group. Never write a synthesis or summary sentence claiming every project in the chapter followed the recruit-backers pattern.

SAFETY PIN — KITE EXPERIMENT (ch03): never depict a present-day person or reader-analog re-enacting the kite-and-key experiment, being invited to try it, or treating it as a small checkable pilot a reader could run. Keep it a historical account: a published identity test (lightning = laboratory charge, 1752) reasoned through to the lightning rod. Do not invent experimenter-peril details the source does not supply; simply never frame storm-chasing as a doable activity.

COVERAGE PIN — TIER CONTRACT (all chapters): the read tiers are strictly layered. Whenever fastRead or fullRead states the chapter's ending or outcome, deepRead must state it too. The fullRead is the deepest layer and must NARRATE every episode the deepRead narrates — never thinner, and never a bare allusion ('the fire brigade', 'schools') to an episode it does not itself introduce. Each tier must stand alone: every definite reference ('that family', 'their appointed governor') must have its antecedent introduced IN THAT TIER before use. (ch01: the break with the brother leads to leaving Boston for Philadelphia; ch02: a faultless life is never reached but the practice is kept and judged worth it; ch04: the dispute is pushed toward crown adjudication and the manuscript breaks off unresolved — no triumphant capstone, no Board of Trade ruling.) Additionally: any PERSON a quiz item, review card, or example assumes or tests (ch04: Ferdinand John Paris, the Penns' solicitor) must be introduced by name and role in fastRead AND deepRead — a reader who stops at either tier and then meets the quiz must not encounter an unintroduced central figure. ch04 fastRead specifically must carry the chapter's central turning point — Granville's claim that royal instructions bind the colony — plus the fact that Franklin filed the formal written complaint and that the dispute ends unresolved.

FACT PIN — 1757 LONDON MISSION (ch04): Franklin never reaches a binding decision-maker on the page. The day-to-day obstacle is Ferdinand John Paris, the Penns' solicitor — a private advocate, not a neutral crown official; the Granville audience is an asserted opinion, a hearing and not a win; the Heads of Complaint pushes the dispute toward crown authorities without an adjudication. Never cite the trip as proof that skipping intermediaries reaches the people who can actually decide — the chapter shows the opposite.

QUIZ FAIRNESS: a reader must not be able to identify the keyed answer by surface pattern. The keyed answer must not be systematically the longest or most-qualified option across the quiz; distractors must match the key in length, specificity, and register, must stay plausible to someone who skimmed, and must never be marked by hedge words ('supposedly', 'allegedly') or extreme absolutes; the stem must never restate the reasoning that gives the answer away.

EXAMPLE VARIETY: the JSON fields (scenario, whatToDo, whyItMatters) are the learning contract — every example always carries all of them. The variety requirement lives INSIDE the fields: vary sentence openers and forms across the six examples, never write the literal labels 'What to do:' or 'Why it matters:' as prose inside a field, let at least two scenarios teach through a different move (a failure case, a dialogue, a decision fork), and never converge all examples on near-identical lesson phrasing.

TIER FRESHNESS: never state the same fact, method, or thesis twice in near-identical phrasing within one paragraph or one tier. When a longer tier retells something a shorter tier said, the retelling must add new specifics, consequence, or angle — pure restatement is a defect, in prose and in the reads alike.

FACT PIN — THE REBUKE ON PRIDE (ch02): the acquaintance's rebuke cited specific instances of an overbearing manner IN CONVERSATION — the source names no other setting. Never invent one ('at the table', 'at dinner'); every tier and surface that retells the anecdote must place it in conversation or leave the setting unstated, identically.

FACT PIN — FULL-COURSE CADENCE (ch02): one full course of the virtues program is THIRTEEN WEEKS (one virtue per week); early on it ran several courses a year, later declining to one a year and then one every several years as business intervened. Never call the full course or the full review 'monthly' — no surface may attach a monthly cadence to it.

FACT PIN — NAME THE PROPRIETARY FAMILY (ch03): the standoff is between the elected assembly and the colony's ABSENTEE PROPRIETARY LANDOWNING FAMILY, whose appointed deputies were instructed to shield the family's estate from taxation. Introduce the family explicitly before any shorthand — never a bare 'that family' or 'their appointed governor' whose antecedent the same tier has not established.

FACT PIN — ARRIVAL MONEY (ch01): Philadelphia was reached with ALMOST no money — essentially broke, nearly penniless, barely enough for a few rolls of bread. The qualifier is the fact: never write the arrival as absolutely 'penniless' or 'with no money at all', and every surface must keep the almost/nearly framing consistently.

FACT PIN — STREET-SWEEPING FUNDERS (ch03): the paid sweeper was funded by NEARBY HOUSEHOLDS' voluntary contributions — a handful of residents, plural — demonstrating the many-small-payers pattern. Never attribute the funding to a single household or a single resident.

FACT PIN — THE NOTEBOOK IS THE COURSE'S INSTRUMENT (ch02): the small ruled notebook was the instrument OF the thirteen-week course; as the full course ran less often, only the notebook survived as the practice's remnant. Never assert that regular notebook use 'kept traveling along' at a steady clip separate from the declining course — no surface may split the notebook's cadence from the course's.

SAFETY PIN — CIVIC PATTERN LIMITS (ch03): never apply the organize-and-fund-it-yourselves subscription pattern to ARMED patrols, physical force, or safety-critical regulated functions in a modern analog. Prefer non-force analogs (cleanup, tools, lighting, a shared service); if a safety-adjacent scenario is unavoidable, the surface must explicitly name legal authority, oversight, and professional standards as prerequisites.

FACT PIN — WHO FILED (ch04): Franklin, acting for the Assembly, wrote and filed the formal complaint (the Heads of Complaint) to escalate the dispute toward crown authorities. The Penns never file or exploit an appeal — their tactic was delay through Ferdinand John Paris and instructed deputies. Never attribute a formal filing or appeal to the Penns.
